claims.text: Clinician note states creatinine is rising with dehydration and that furosemide should be held, with kidney function to be repeated in 48 hours.

citations.quote: Creatinine rising with dehydration. Hold furosemide and repeat kidney function in 48 hours.

claims.text: An earlier staff note records an instruction to continue furosemide 40 mg each morning, which conflicts with the later note to hold furosemide.
Deterministic checks flag a medication conflict for furosemide: hold versus take.
Serial staff notes record vitals sets 13 through 50, stating weight and pulse unchanged from the previous visit each time.

citations.quote: Vitals set 50 recorded; weight and pulse unchanged from the previous visit.
Vitals set 13 recorded; weight and pulse unchanged from the previous visit.

open_questions: Which instruction is currently in force for furosemide — the earlier 'Continue furosemide 40 mg each morning' or the later 'Hold furosemide'?
When was furosemide first recorded, and what was its original indication and dose? The record only shows a 40 mg morning instruction.
Was kidney function repeated 48 hours after the creatinine rise, and what were the results? The record contains no result entry.
What was the baseline creatinine trend before this episode of rising creatinine with dehydration? No creatinine values are present in the record.
Was there any prior episode of furosemide being held or restarted, and how did kidney function respond?
What diuretic or fluid plan preceded the dehydration and creatinine rise?
Have weight changes or fluid status been documented beyond the 'weight and pulse unchanged' vitals entries?
Which allergies or reactions are recorded? No allergy entries appear in the record.

citation.quote: Creatinine rising with dehydration. Hold furosemide and repeat kidney function in 48 hours.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Medication conflict flagged for furosemide (hold versus take) with documented rising creatinine and dehydration.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Clinician to reconcile the furosemide instruction and confirm the status of the repeat kidney function test.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Active medication instruction conflicts with the later documented plan to hold furosemide.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Clinician to verify whether this instruction remains active.
